stemBlocks.value: On the same axes used in Question 1, draw the graph of x = −3 and state the coordinates of the point at which the two lines intersect.
Think first: The line y = 4 is already drawn; x = −3 is the other kind of line, and where they cross is fixed by both equations at once.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p067-q05 from workbook page 67.

contentBlocks.value: x = −3 places no condition on y, so y may take any value
A vertical straight line through the x-axis at −3, covering the full height of the grid
The point must satisfy both x = −3 and y = 4

strategyBlocks.value: Draw x = −3 as a vertical line, then read off the point where it meets the horizontal line y = 4.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x = −3 is a vertical line 3 units to the left of the y-axis. The two lines intersect at (−3, 4).

whyThisWorks.value: A point of intersection is the one place where both equations are true at the same time. Here y = 4 fixes the height and x = −3 fixes the horizontal position, so together they pin down exactly one point. This is the graphical meaning of solving a pair of equations simultaneously, and it works the same way for slanted lines.
